Consequently service forecast records and all Quant lifecycle events identify the executing implementation as attempt 1 instead of the active and candidate accepted attempt 3.
blocking_issues.contract_basis: The Observability contract requires stage, stage revision, attempt and agent metadata where available. The active workflow supplies attempt 3, and control-plane closure must bind one accepted implementation/Observability/QA/Review chain for the same attempt. Publishing attempt 1 from a product implementation changed in attempt 3 makes runtime provenance stale and ambiguous.
blocking_issues.impact: Downstream Stage 08 and later audit/debug consumers cannot reliably associate forecast output or lifecycle telemetry with the implementation artifact that introduced the canonical-label repair and produced the accepted model milestones.
blocking_issues.required_disposition: Start a non-overwriting Stage 07 retry, update the locked Quant runtime identity and its direct tests/artifacts to the current implementation attempt, then rerun Observability and QA. Preserve all prior attempt artifacts.
